headline: Recommended starting council meetings at 5:30 p.m. and asked the city manager to consider a budget priority process.
summary: Council meetings would start at 5:30 p.m., and public comment would run up to 60 minutes. Proposed rules 61, 62 and 63 were filed, and a chairman's order asks the city manager to consider a budget priority process. Rule 5 on special meetings was kept as is.
decisions: Approved a chairman's order asking the city manager to consider a council budget priority process, 3-0.
Filed item 3A, the communication on proposed Rules 61, 62 and 63, 3-0.
Recommended amending Rule 4 to start council meetings at 5:30 p.m. and Rule 39 to allow 60 minutes of public participation, 3-0.
Recommended filing the item on Rule 5 about special meetings with no change to the rule, 3-0.
Filed item 4C on Rule 35 and approved a chairman's order asking that it be applied to all councilors, 3-0.
discussion: Proposed Rules 61 to 63: Councilors wanted an earlier say in budget choices, while the finance office said revenue and state aid numbers come too late for early requests.
Council meeting start time: Councilors weighed a 5:30 p.m. start against a 6:30 p.m. public comment period, and speakers said a 5:30 p.m. start would keep some workers from attending.
Rule 35 enforcement: Councilors said the rule, which limits speaking on an order to those who want to amend, oppose, or question it, should be enforced the same way for everyone.
Special meetings rule: Councilors said the five-member petition rule for special meetings has rarely come up, and they saw no reason to change it.
